# Wild Pokémon: Pokémon Sapphire NDS

Every area with wild Pokémon, as the game has them. The tables are Sapphire's own (from the pokeruby decompilation), with the same odds per slot.
Levels above 24 are raised to go with the Exp. Share (levels up to 24 are unchanged), so the levels here are the ones you meet.

- Each rod fishes its own table, as in Gen 3: the Old Rod, the Good Rod and the Super Rod.
- Rock Smash: breaking a rock sometimes starts a battle, as in Gen 3.
- Percentages add up the slots of the same Pokémon.
- **After the Champion** (from your first Hall of Fame on), some areas use a second table, marked "after the Champion": the other versions' Pokémon take some of their slots, so you can catch them without trading ([completing the Pokédex](postgame-sapphire.md#completing-the-pokédex)).
- **Safari Zone:** its areas are a game with its own rules ([Safari Zone rules](#safari-zone-rules)).
- **Pokémon from other regions** (YES to Professor Birch's eighth question, or the lab worker in Birch's lab: [options](options.md)): Pokémon from Sinnoh and Unova (Gen 4 and 5) take some of the slots in most areas, usually about a quarter of the encounters there (5% to 31% of a grass or surfing table). Those tables come after the area's own ones and are marked "with Pokémon from other regions"; without that option, the area's own tables apply. The Old Rod is never changed. Some of them change again after the Champion (marked "with Pokémon from other regions, after the Champion").
- **The Gen 4 and 5 starters** are in the wild with that option, very rare, one area each:

| Pokémon | Where | How | Chance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chimchar | [Route 112](#route-112) | grass | 1% |
| Oshawott | [Petalburg City](#petalburg-city) | surfing | 1% |
| Piplup | [Route 103](#route-103) | grass | 1% |
| Snivy | [Route 116](#route-116) | grass | 1% |
| Tepig | [Route 113](#route-113) | grass | 1% |
| Turtwig | [Petalburg Woods](#petalburg-woods) | grass | 1% |

## Safari Zone rules

The Safari Zone, north of Route 121, is a game as in Gen 3:

- **Entering:** the gate on Route 121 charges $500 and gives you 30 Safari Balls. You need the Pokéblock Case, and with a full party a free place in your PC's Boxes (a Pokémon you catch goes there).
- **The game** lasts 500 steps. It is over when you have walked them ("Ding-dong! Time's up! Your Safari Game is over.") or when your Safari Balls run out: after the battle in which you threw the last one ("You've run out of Safari Balls. Your Safari Game is over."), or at once when the last one misses ("Announcer: You're out of Safari Balls! Game over!"). Then you are back at the gate. The attendant by the door inside lets you leave sooner.
- **Leftover Safari Balls** are taken back when the game ends. Flying away or using Teleport ends the game too, and takes the balls.
- **Battles** are Gen 3's Safari battles: your Pokémon stay in their balls, and each turn you choose one of four things:
  - **Ball** throws a Safari Ball. It works 1.5 times as well as a Poké Ball, as in Gen 3, and the wild Pokémon is always at full health, so Pokémon that are easy to catch anywhere are easy here.
  - **Pokéblock** opens your Pokéblock Case: pick a Pokéblock and throw it. A Pokémon whose nature likes its flavours is enthralled (for example "Oddish is enthralled by the Sweet Pokéblock!") and becomes much less likely to run away; one that doesn't mind it is curious ("Oddish is curious about the Sweet Pokéblock!") and becomes less likely to run away; one that dislikes it ignores it ("Oddish completely ignored the Sweet Pokéblock!"), and nothing changes. The Pokéblock is used up. In a battle each throw helps a little less than the one before, down to the third; later ones help as much as that one. Closing the Case without throwing one costs no turn.
  - **Go Near** ("You crept closer to Oddish!") makes the Pokémon easier to catch (by less each time) but more likely to run away. After the third try you can't get any closer ("You can't get any closer!"), though each try still makes it a little easier to catch and more likely to run away, as in Gen 3.
  - **Run** leaves the battle. It always works.
- **The wild Pokémon** watches you after your turn, or runs away: 15% of the time at first. Go Near and Pokéblocks change that from the next turn on. As in Gen 3, a Pokéblock that takes away exactly what is left of that chance makes the Pokémon stop running away at all, until you Go Near.
- **The DexNav** works here too: a search costs only the steps you walk, its Pokémon are Safari battles like the others, and a Pokémon you catch keeps what the DexNav gave it (its IVs, egg move, hidden ability or shininess).
